title: Round 9 (vs Haiku's round 1): a station without a train
model: Skippy Core's coder (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, MTP, Q8) as a vanilla agent (Claude Code with purple's system prompt, an empty setup, effort high, a 131K window) plus purple's generic help: the eyes, the stop gate's work check (MineBench's runtime as the checker, the renderer as the viewer, an 80K output-token budget) and its fix-the-worst-fault loop (Core's big model reviews each new version's picture against the task and names the worst fault; the coder is sent back to fix it until none is left, five sends at most)
verdict: Haiku won, blind. The coder's build is a row of sheds and roofs beside a track with a small grey engine lost among them; Haiku's is a steam train with smoke and three coaches on a landscaped base. One fault send (floating flue tubes), fixed; the review then passed it.
